resolved_conflicts.explanation: Not resolved. The 1948 newspaper item says the tower was wood; the 1964 NGS description says a metal cab on steel channel legs. The story reports both and does not choose between them.

Not resolved. The 1948 item puts the tower five and one-half miles north of Youngstown; the 1964 NGS station is about four miles north at the US 231 and SR 20 junction. The record does not show whether these describe the same structure.

notes_for_editor: The brief's blow-down date, registration and agency check out against FFLOS. The history rests on two 1940s-era newspaper items and a 1964 NGS station description, all read through the Forest Lookouts transcription rather than the originals. The 1948 and 1964 accounts conflict on material and distance (see resolved_conflicts). A 2014 News Herald article (search snippet only; the fetch returned 403) says a Youngstown forest ranger still went up the Bay County tower when alerted; if it can be read from another route it may support a staffing sentence. The brief's access 'unknown' is left unfilled; no source states an access level.
